meta.title: Ukrainian Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 135 expressions · 62 everyday, 68 idioms, 5 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 135 Ukrainian set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 62 everyday phrases, 68 idioms and 5 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Ukrainian → English (see the Ukrainian, recall the meaning) and English → Ukrainian (see an English meaning, recall the Ukrainian) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Ukrainian A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases and does not mark as idiomatic — mostly the everyday formulas a Ukrainian speaker uses as one piece (чи не так, а що, як справи …), with the greetings of the festivals and the national salute. The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (мене звати, накласти на себе руки, в руках …), and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (всі дороги ведуть до Риму, гроші не пахнуть, раз та гаразд …); Wiktionary files many more Ukrainian sayings as idioms than as proverbs, and they are left where it puts them. Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Ukrainian sentences contain them, an expression with a verb being counted in any form of that verb; only 67 of the 135 are found there at all, and the rest follow in the order of how common their words are in film and television subtitles. Every expression is printed in Cyrillic with its stress marked. Real example sentences come with 63 of the 135 expressions, three apiece for 30, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings, stress and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR.
